gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Wayne's ESP25 backup pump does not work unless two check valves are fitted, one on the primary pump's discharge and one on the backup's, and neither comes in the box. Wayne also sizes the ESP25's battery box for a 12 V sealed lead-acid battery no bigger than a group 27, and names its WSB1275 75 Ah battery as the one to buy.
standout_why: I opened ChatGPT's three cited pages: the Consumer Reports buying guide, its duplicate URL, and the Consumer Reports Best Sump Pump Backup Systems page. They say backup pumps share the primary's discharge line and take a 12-volt deep-cycle battery sold separately, and they tell readers to 'consult the pump manufacturer's recommendations'. None of them mentions check valves for battery units, a battery group size, a fit limit for the battery box, or Wayne's named battery. Without the second check valve the kit fails, because water loops back into the pit. I did not open the uncited results (SSPMA, ICLR, Ferguson, Angi and others), so one of them may cover check valves in general terms. That is why this is a 2 and not a 3.
kit_items: Backup pump: Wayne ESP25, the 12 V add-on unit ChatGPT showed for homes that already have a working primary pump. It plumbs in-line on 1-1/4 in. or 1-1/2 in. rigid PVC. The pump outlet is 1-1/2 in. NPT, so a 1-1/4 in. line needs an adapter that is not included.

Battery: Wayne WSB1275 75 Ah maintenance-free battery. Wayne's ESP25 page recommends it by name, and the manual says the oversize case holds a 12 V SLA battery up to a 27-frame size. Don't swap in a 12 V LiFePO4 such as the Vatrer or Redodo batteries Dealectric lists: Wayne's manual only describes sealed lead-acid, and its charger is not documented for lithium.

Check valves ×2: one on the main AC pump's discharge and one on the ESP25's line. Wayne says the system 'will not function without two check valves'. Its Method 1 calls for a rubber check valve (sold separately), sized to the 1-1/4 or 1-1/2 in. pipe.
Outlet: a GFCI-protected 115 VAC outlet on its own fuse, within six feet of the sump, for the charger/control box. This is an install requirement, not something to buy.

findings.label: Check valves the system needs
findings.value: 2 (one on the main AC pump's discharge, one on the backup pump's)
findings.source_title: Wayne ESP25 Operating Instructions & Parts Manual, Control Box Installation (mirror of Wayne form 352207-001 01/14)
findings.note: Manual text: 'A check valve will be required in the discharge line of BOTH the Main AC pump and the back-up pump' and 'System will not function without two check valves.' Page 2 of the same manual calls the check valve 'sold separately'. Read on a manualslib mirror because Wayne's own PDF was not reachable.

findings.label: Battery type and largest size that fits
findings.source_title: Wayne ESP25 Operating Instructions & Parts Manual (form 352207-001 01/14, © 2014 WAYNE/Scott Fetzer)
findings.note: The manual says the system 'is designed to operate most efficiently with sealed lead acid (SLA) batteries' and that the included oversize case 'will accommodate a 12-volt SLA battery (up to a 27-frame size)'. It does not mention lithium.

findings.label: Battery Wayne recommends
findings.value: Wayne WSB1275, 75 Ah maintenance-free, sold separately
findings.source_title: Wayne ESP25 12 Volt Reinforced Thermoplastic Battery Back Up System (maker product page)
findings.note: The maker's page says '12V battery required' and recommends the WSB1275.

findings.label: Discharge pipe the pump fits
findings.value: 1-1/4 in. or 1-1/2 in. rigid PVC; 1-1/2 in. NPT pump outlet; 1-1/4 in. adapter not included
findings.source_title: Wayne ESP25 Operating Instructions & Parts Manual, installation page
findings.note: 'Pump must be installed using 1 1/4" or 1 1/2" rigid PVC piping'; 'If a 1 1/4" discharge pipe is desired, an adapter (not included) will be necessary.'

findings.label: Float switch mounting height
findings.value: at least 10–12 in. above the bottom of the sump pit, above the main pump's normal 'on' level
findings.source_title: Wayne ESP25 Operating Instructions & Parts Manual, Control Box Installation
findings.note: Set this way, the backup only starts if the primary fails or can't keep up.

findings.label: Flow at 10 ft lift
findings.value: 1,680 GPH (2,900 GPH at 0 ft, 600 GPH at 15 ft)

findings.label: Battery and charger placement
findings.value: battery within 6 ft of the sump, next to a separately fused 115 VAC GFCI outlet
findings.source_title: Wayne ESP25 Operating Instructions & Parts Manual
findings.note: The manual also warns that reversed battery cables can damage the control box and void the warranty.

findings.label: Systems it does not fit
findings.value: not compatible with older Basement Watchdog Special (BWSP), Big Dog (BWD12-120C) or Big Combination (BW4000); compatible with BWE, DFK961, CITE-33, BWSP+, BWD12-120C+, BW4000/CITS-50
findings.source_title: Do it Best: The Basement Watchdog Maintenance Free AGM Standby Sump Pump Battery, Model #BW-27AGM
findings.note: This is a retailer page, not the maker's: basementwatchdog.com's AGM battery page returned 404. It matters for ChatGPT's Basement Watchdog Special card: the controller must be the '+' version to take the AGM battery.

unsourced: Amazon prices and listing URLs for the Wayne ESP25, the WSB1275 and the check valves: amzcheck.py returned blocked:true for every ASIN and empty results for every search, so I did not open any Amazon listing. Note that none of the approved brand stores (BLUETTI, Vatrer, Redodo and the rest) sells a sump pump, so Amazon is the only cart that could hold this kit.

A statement from Wayne that the ESP25 charger accepts or rejects LiFePO4 batteries: Wayne's ESP25 page and the 2014 manual describe only SLA. I could not read Wayne's own PDF manuals (PDF text extraction needed approval in this session), and Wayne publishes no lithium statement that I could find.
The WSB1275's group size and dimensions on a Wayne page: the ESP25 page names the WSB1275 as a 75 Ah battery but gives no group size.
The maker's own Basement Watchdog page on battery compatibility and lithium: basementwatchdog.com/products/agm-battery/ returned 404, and the only sources I found were retailers.
Whether the uncited results (SSPMA backup sump system PDF, ICLR booklets, Ferguson, Angi, SEC America) already state the two-check-valve requirement: I did not open them within the tool budget.
